column1: Fourteen days since the convoy incident. The Argo has been running standard operations in the meantime, focusing on a short return to the more normal. Suddenly the HPG relay activates. Incoming transmission using the Tribe's encryption, with priority flagging. Darius brings it up on the main display. Joanna McEvedy appears, but something has changed. Her expression is colder, harder. Even less patience than usual in her eyes, much more steel. "Commander {COMMANDER.Callsign}. The re-verification of all my intelligence agents is finished. My network has been secured and purged of Ghost Bear infiltration." She leans forward slightly, intensity radiating from the screen. "But the time for careful, surgical strikes has passed. Ghost Bear Watch has escalated their operations across the entire Periphery. They're not just hunting warriors anymore. They're targeting families. Elders. Children. Anyone with Wolverine blood or Tribe connections." "They're doing to us what they did in 2824 when they annihilated Clan Wolverine. Systematic extermination disguised as counter-terrorism. We will not allow history to repeat itself." Her voice drops to something darker, more zealous. "They tried to erase us from history. They hunted our ancestors to extinction. Now we'll dismantle their capacity to hunt us. Every Ghost Bear institution that has participated in operations against Minnesota Tribe will answer for centuries of persecution. This is justice for all the lost Wolverines of the past." "I'm attaching our latest intelligence package now. Verified through multiple independent sources. You'll see the pattern of Ghost Bear escalation across the Periphery." Farah pauses the transmission and pulls up the incoming data package. "Commander, confirming data reception. Large intelligence file, multiple operational summaries, prisoner manifests, facility locations." She scans through the files quickly. "Initial review shows consistency with Joanna's claims about Ghost Bear operations. Reports of raids on suspected Tribe locations, detention of civilians, increased Watch activity in frontier systems." She looks up, expression cautious. "But I'll need time to verify this independently. Cross-reference with public records, compare with known Ghost Bear deployment patterns. We should be certain of its accuracy before we act." Darius nods. "Good. Resume the transmission. Let's hear what she wants." Farah reactivates the feed. Joanna continues without pause. "Our first priority is immediate. Ghost Bear Watch maintains a secret detention facility in the St. Andreas system. They're holding Minnesota Tribe operatives captured during recent operations." She pulls up a prisoner manifest on her display. "Two confirmed Tribe personnel. Pilots, intelligence officers, logistics coordinators. Our people. They've been classified as 'terrorists and war criminals' by Ghost Bear command. They're still under trial, but we don't expect a fair ruling and their execution will occur soon." "We will not abandon our own to Ghost Bear justice. You are to transit to St. Andreas, breach the detention facility, and extract all Minnesota Tribe operatives. Secondary objective is to extract all prisoners flagged as 'Tribe-affiliated' by our intelligence network." Facility schematics appear on the transmission. "Expected opposition is heavy. Heavy and assault mechs highly likely, several lances worth. The facility is hardened and prepared for potential rescue attempts. This will be a quite difficult operation. I will send some support units to rendezvous with you during the mission. This means you need to immediately deploy on arrival, or they will expedite the execution as soon as they spot our forces moving in." Her voice turns to ice. "This facility has already held our people for months. They've been interrogated, tortured, psychologically broken. Ghost Bear 'justice' means eventual execution for anyone with Wolverine connections, but never a fast end to the suffering. We extract our own, Commander. Always. Bring them home." The transmission pauses. Darius immediately pulls up the mission data. "Boss, this is heavily defended. Prison break operations are always high-risk, but this one is serious. We're looking at assault-class opposition in a fortified position." Yang reviews the facility schematics. "Fortified position, overlapping turret coverage, prepared defensive positions. They're expecting a rescue attempt. Someone tipped them off or they're just paranoid. Either way, this won't be easy." Sumire analyzes the prisoner manifest. "Two Minnesota Tribe operatives with documented capture records. Names, ranks, specializations all listed. But there's a secondary list of those three prisoners flagged as 'Tribe-affiliated.' The identifications on these seem less certain. They are marked as 'suspected troublemakers' or 'possible Tribe sympathizers.'" Joanna's voice cuts back in. "Extract everyone marked on that manifest, Commander. We cannot leave potential allies or sympathizers to Ghost Bear interrogation. They'll break anyone eventually." The crew exchanges glances. No one speaks, but the look is clear. Something feels different about this. Sumire pulls up system data. "St. Andreas system. Single inhabited world, St. Timalin. Periphery colony world, population approximately four million. Primary terrain is temperate forests and grasslands with scattered urban centers." "The detention facility is located in a remote region, approximately two hundred kilometers from the nearest civilian settlement. Isolated by design for security purposes." "Historical note. St. Timalin was settled during the late Star League era. No significant military importance, primarily agricultural and light manufacturing economy." Darius looks to you. "Boss, rescuing prisoners of war is legitimate military action. Her own people are in that facility facing execution. But Joanna's tone has changed. She's talking about historical justice, repaying centuries-old debts. That's not the language of a defensive operation." Yang grunts. "Mission's still solid though. Extract captured operatives before they're executed. That's the job. Whatever Joanna's personal motivations are, the mission makes sense." Sumire calculates transit time. "St. Andreas is distant. We're looking at multiple jumps, several weeks of travel time. We should begin preparations immediately if we're accepting this contract." Farah still looks troubled but nods. "I'll continue verifying the intelligence package during transit. If there are discrepancies, I hope to detect them before we engage."

"We will not abandon our own to Ghost Bear justice. You are to transit to St. Andreas, breach the detention facility, and extract all Minnesota Tribe operatives. Secondary objective is to extract all prisoners flagged as 'Tribe-affiliated' by our intelligence network." Facility schematics appear on the transmission. "Expected opposition is heavy. Heavy and assault mechs highly likely, several lances worth. The facility is hardened and prepared for potential rescue attempts. This will be a quite difficult operation. I will send some support units to rendezvous with you during the mission. This means you need to immediately deploy on arrival, or they will expedite the execution as soon as they spot our forces moving in." Her voice turns to ice. "This facility has already held our people for months. They've been interrogated, tortured, psychologically broken. Ghost Bear 'justice' means eventual execution for anyone with Wolverine connections, but never a fast end to the suffering. We extract our own, Commander. Always. Bring them home." The transmission pauses. Darius immediately pulls up the mission data. "Boss, this is heavily defended. Prison break operations are always high-risk, but this one is serious. We're looking at assault-class opposition in a fortified position." Yang reviews the facility schematics. "Fortified position, overlapping turret coverage, prepared defensive positions. They're expecting a rescue attempt. Someone tipped them off or they're just paranoid. Either way, this won't be easy." Sumire analyzes the prisoner manifest. "Two Minnesota Tribe operatives with documented capture records. Names, ranks, specializations all listed. But there's a secondary list of those three prisoners flagged as 'Tribe-affiliated.' The identifications on these seem less certain. They are marked as 'suspected troublemakers' or 'possible Tribe sympathizers.'" Joanna's voice cuts back in. "Extract everyone marked on that manifest, Commander. We cannot leave potential allies or sympathizers to Ghost Bear interrogation. They'll break anyone eventually." The crew exchanges glances. No one speaks, but the look is clear. Something feels different about this. Sumire pulls up system data. "St. Andreas system. Single inhabited world, St. Timalin. Periphery colony world, population approximately four million. Primary terrain is temperate forests and grasslands with scattered urban centers." "The detention facility is located in a remote region, approximately two hundred kilometers from the nearest civilian settlement. Isolated by 设计 for security purposes." "Historical note. St. Timalin was settled during the late Star League era. No significant military importance, primarily agricultural and light manufacturing economy." Darius looks to you. "Boss, rescuing prisoners of war is legitimate military action. Her own people are in that facility facing execution. But Joanna's tone has changed. She's talking about historical justice, repaying centuries-old debts. That's not the language of a defensive operation." Yang grunts. "Mission's still solid though. Extract captured operatives before they're executed. That's the job. Whatever Joanna's personal motivations are, the mission makes sense." Sumire calculates transit time. "St. Andreas is distant. We're looking at multiple jumps, several weeks of travel time. We should begin preparations immediately if we're accepting this contract." Farah still looks troubled but nods. "I'll continue verifying the intelligence package during transit. If there are discrepancies, I hope to detect them before we engage."

column1: In the Argo's command deck, final checks scroll across every screen. Supplies are loaded. Mechbays sealed. The navmap shows a jagged arc of jumps leading rimward, through ghost systems, salvage worlds, and quiet stars barely catalogued. Sumire frowns at the plotted course. "We'll be lucky if half the stations we refuel at even have working lights." Darius mutters, "If Jorgensson's intel is right, we're heading straight into the mouth of something that's been brewing for decades." Yang doesn't look up from his screen. "Then let's not keep it waiting." Melidron is far away, beyond the reach of most traders, far from any safe harbor. But the coordinates are set, the time to go is now.

column1: It arrives quietly. No fanfare. No signatures. A Union-class drop shuttle sets down on the far side of the Dunianshire VI logistics pad, logged under a clearly fake manifest. The pilot doesn't disembark. Just waits while a series of sealed containers are offloaded and moved aboard the Argo by contract haulers who don't speak a word. The crew gathers in the hangar as the crates are pried open. Inside the crates, the crew finds two full pallets stacked with hard-case C-Bills in untraceable denominations. Nestled beside them are several weapons case, foam-lined and without markings. The last container is heavier. An old, reinforced pressure case bearing faded [[DM.Factions[faction_SLDF],SLDF]] inventory codes. Farah eyes it immediately, already murmuring that she'll need time to analyze whatever's inside. Tucked between two crates, on plain cardstock: "Best regards, AJ." That's all. No instructions. No authorization codes. Just enough to suggest a very deliberate silence. Darius scowls, folding his arms. "So… that's what a payoff looks like." Yang gives a low grunt. "She's buying our quiet. And not even being subtle about it." Farah doesn't speak. She just stares at the SLDF container with quiet intensity. Sumire half-smiles. "You know... the Tribe never sent us hush money. Maybe we picked the wrong side." She pauses. Looks around. "...Kidding. Probably." The tension doesn't break. You can feel it. Uncertainty creeping in at the edges of the crew. About the war. About Arelle. About what comes next. For now, everyone returns to their stations. But the quiet isn't just silence. It's doubt.

column1: It's been nearly a month since Arelle confirmed it. The Minnesota Tribe is real. Not a ghost story. Not a tech myth. Real, and in motion. The Argo's crew has had time to breathe, plan, resupply. But no one truly relaxed. Now, a priority hyperpulse message hits the buffer, encrypted in Ghost Bear protocols. It decrypts in seconds. Short and sharp. "Return to Melidron at once. Situation has changed. Details can not be shared over hyperpulse." - Star Colonel Arelle Jorgensson Sumire lowers the screen, visibly uneasy. "Hell of a tone for a summons." Darius shifts in his seat, arms crossed. "Could be new intel. Could be a trap. We've pissed off a lot of powerful people lately." Farah just nods grimly. "Something's about to break loose. I can feel it."

column1: Just as you are about to settle for a peaceful dinner in the messhall, a high-priority message arrives. Holo-headers mark it as official correspondence from the [[TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef,{TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef.Demonym}]] Office of Planetary Oversight on Dunianshire VI. The speaker is a tall, sharp-featured woman dressed in a rose-gold {TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef.Demonym} bureaucrat's uniform. Polished, poised, and clearly reading from a prepared script. "To the command of {COMPANY.CompanyName}, You are formally notified that your unit initiated unsanctioned combat operations within the territorial jurisdiction of the {TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef.Name}. Planetary authorities have received multiple reports indicating your forces engaged what appears to be a licensed independent security contractor under false pretense. Effective immediately, a provisional lien in the amount of 4 billion C-Bills is being placed against your organization pending full investigation. - Senior Attaché Halyn Vorelli." The feed ends. No negotiation. No recourse. Darius lets out a low whistle. "That's... extortion with extra steps." Farah frowns over the tactical data from the mission. "The entire [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]] force was running in complete false flag mode, transponders, colors. Even the mech chassis numbers. I could see why someone would be fooled by this." Sumire leans against the console. "Four billion? That's not a fine, that's what you'd charge for glassing a city." Yang scoffs. "They don't want money. They want us scared enough to start talking." The timing's no accident. Someone in {TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef.ShortName} suspects there's more to this fight than mercs shooting mercs. They just don't know what it is, and they're desperate to learn. But it is strange. The local government should have been informed by Arelle by now. There's only one person who'll know the answer. It's time to contact Arelle.

column1: Mizuki's voice cuts through a wall of static, sharp and unwavering. "Outpost Eleven is under threat. [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Watch]] strike groups are advancing on multiple fronts, and we must act before the entire sector collapses." She gestures toward a grainy tactical map, flickering red symbols crawl across the screen, surrounding key [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]] positions. "One target is our elite combat cadre, still running drills in the field. If they're overrun, we lose the warriors trained to lead the next generation." "Another is a buried ruin. Our engineers uncovered forgotten simulator tech beneath it. The Ghost Bears are moving to destroy everything before we can extract it." "And the last is our main training facility itself. They're sending everything at it. This is no raid. It's extermination." She locks eyes with you. "You'll handle all three. This is just choosing which to strike first. Once a mission is issued, you have 14 days to complete it. And each success will earn you a special reward, custom systems, rare salvage, assets we don't hand out lightly." The transmission flickers out. The screen waits, silent and blinking, for your decision.

column1: Several days have passed since Liberation Day. The three Ghost Bear civilians are gone, transferred to Joanna's custody along with the two rescued Tribe operatives who kept talking about purges and blood debts. The crew hasn't spoken much about any of it since the transfer, but the atmosphere aboard the Argo remains tense and uncertain. Everyone's working, performing their duties with professional efficiency, but the easy camaraderie that used to fill the corridors has been replaced by something more strained. The HPG relay activates with an incoming transmission using Tribe encryption protocols. Joanna McEvedy appears on the viewscreen, her expression focused and professional, all business today with no trace of the zealotry that colored her previous communications. Her tone is tactical, efficient, matter-of-fact. "Commander [[COMMANDER.LastName,{COMMANDER.LastName}]]. We've identified a high-value target that requires immediate action. The [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bear Watch]] maintains a forward intelligence post in a remote region of St. Andreas that coordinates surveillance of [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]] movements across the entire Periphery sector. This installation has been tracking our cell locations, monitoring our communications, and feeding precise targeting data to Watch strike teams for months." She transmits tactical data to the main display, showing facility schematics and regional maps. "Our intelligence network has identified a narrow operational window where the garrison will be at reduced strength due to a scheduled rotation cycle. Your objective is to capture the facility intact and extract all intelligence data from their computer systems before Watch command can initiate remote purge protocols. We need to know the full scope of their surveillance operations against our people. The data inside those servers could reveal Watch operational plans against dozens of our cells across the sector and potentially save hundreds of lives." "Expected opposition includes standard garrison forces protecting the installation, nothing beyond typical military resistance. The location is remote and isolated from major population centers, which means minimal risk of third-party interference or civilian complications during the operation." She pauses, meeting the camera directly with an expression of professional concern. "This intelligence could save lives, Commander. Our people are being hunted systematically because Watch intelligence knows where they are, who they talk to, how they move. This data tells us exactly how they know all of that. It's a defensive operation, not an offensive strike. We need this information to protect our cells from future raids." The transmission ends, leaving silence filling the briefing room as the crew processes what they just heard. Darius pulls up the mission data on his console and reviews it methodically. "This looks like a standard base capture on paper. Military intelligence post, isolated location, and with clear objectives. It's really textbook stuff." He looks up from the display with visible caution in his expression. "But after what we've learned in recent operations, I want independent verification before we commit. Farah, can you cross-reference the facility coordinates against known Watch deployment records and civilian databases during transit? I want to confirm this installation is actually what Joanna says it is." Farah nods slowly, her expression thoughtful and careful. "I can access civilian databases and compare satellite imagery if we have it available. See if the installation profile matches what Joanna's describing in her briefing. It'll take some time to compile everything, but we should have solid answers before we arrive." "The operation itself sounds legitimate from a military standpoint. Capturing enemy intelligence installations is standard warfare doctrine. But given recent discrepancies, I want to verify what we can independently." Yang leans against the wall with his arms crossed, his skepticism plain on his face. "Mission makes sense on paper, I'll give her that. Intelligence post, surveillance data, defensive objective to protect your own people from enemy strikes. That's all textbook legitimate military operations." "But I don't trust anything Joanna sends us anymore without checking it twice, maybe three times. We verify everything before we pull triggers from now on." Sumire brings up navigation data and regional analysis on her console. "Remote location confirmed by independent stellar cartography. Population density in the target region is extremely low, with the nearest civilian settlement located approximately eighty kilometers from the facility coordinates." "The isolation factor works in our favor from a tactical perspective. Limited reinforcement potential for the garrison means we can control the engagement envelope more effectively." Darius reviews the mission parameters one final time before looking up at you. "Boss, this looks clean from every angle I can see. Military target, clear objective, isolated location with minimal civilian risk. Nothing in the briefing suggests questionable targeting or the kind of intelligence problems we've encountered before." "But we verify everything during transit anyway. Farah checks the databases for inconsistencies. I cross-reference Watch deployment patterns against historical records. Sumire analyzes whatever satellite data we can access. We go into this operation with full information this time, not blind trust." The crew exchanges glances around the briefing room, and the tension is palpable despite the apparently legitimate mission parameters. No one is enthusiastic about working for Joanna anymore. No one is eager to accept her intelligence at face value. But no one can identify an obvious problem with this particular operation either. The target appears to be exactly what she claims it is.

<color=#BFBFBF>Shortly after arriving in orbit over {TGT_SYSTEM.Name}, Farah flags a new encrypted packet pushed through the secure [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]] channel Mizuki provided during your first briefing.

Once decrypted, the payload opens to reveal a dense starmap overlay. Thirteen systems, scattered across the deep Rimward Periphery, marked with internal Minnesota Tribe designations. Each one represents a known or previously dormant asset: remote facilities, resource stockpiles, fallback shelters, and research outposts.

These are not battlefield rumors or salvage logs. This is real infrastructure. Real reach. And it's only being shared with your crew now that you've joined their side.

Another entry stands out, a simple statement likely based on your own reports.</color>

<color=#DFDFDF>"System Entry: MELIDRON – Noted under Potential Ghost Bear Watch Occupation"</color>

<color=#BFBFBF>Farah skims the entry, already aligning the rest of the data to jump coordinates and threat overlays.</color> "Alright… syncing them in. Let's see what we're working with."

<color=#BFBFBF>For the first time, you see the scattered edge of the Tribe's real territory, or at last what they are willing to share with a newcomer. But these are no longer myths, no longer rumors. Just stars, waiting to be fought for.</color>

column1: The Argo continues its orbit of Butzfleth Majoris in silence. The mech bay still smells like burned coolant and scorched armor plating. Yang is the first to talk about it, leaning against a bulkhead in the mess hall while the rest of the crew picks at rations. "Prisoners. He was shipping prisoners to build bunkers. People doing forced labor in some frozen hole because a warden decided they were worth more as bodies than as inmates." He shakes his head. "I've worked jobs where the line between contractor and conscript got thin. But this wasn't thin. This was gone." Darius sets down his mug. "The kill was clean. That's not what's bothering me. What's bothering me is whether it actually changes anything. Rooke was the middleman. The Tribe needed labor, he supplied it. We cut him out, they find someone else. Another warden, another frontier governor with a flexible conscience. The demand doesn't go away just because we removed one supplier." Before anyone can respond, Sumire flags an incoming transmission on the bridge console. Another [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bear]] encrypted signal. She reads it aloud. "Rooke is eliminated. Labor flow to the [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]] has ceased. Next target: Cygnus system. Expect hostile activity to be increased. Full mission briefing upon arrival." Sumire stares at the screen for a moment. "Labor flow has ceased. That's how she describes it. Not prisoners freed, not people rescued. Labor flow. Like she turned off a supply line for raw materials." Nobody argues, nobody disagrees.

Another warden, another frontier governor with a flexible conscience. The demand doesn't go away just because we removed one supplier." Before anyone can respond, Sumire flags an incoming transmission on the bridge console. Another [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bear]] encrypted signal. She reads it aloud. "Rooke is eliminated. Labor flow to the [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]] has ceased. Next target: Cygnus system. Expect hostile activity to be increased. Full mission briefing upon arrival." Sumire stares at the screen for a moment. "Labor flow has ceased. That's how she describes it. Not prisoners freed, not people rescued. Labor flow. Like she turned off a supply line for raw materials." Nobody argues, nobody disagrees.

column1: The Argo eases into orbit above Horgens III, the third planet in the Horgens system. Below, the surface brims with equatorial jungles and sprawling lowland basins, heavy with moisture, layered in fog, and riddled with flooded deltas. The planet is still young in colonial terms: minimal infrastructure, scattered settlements clinging to riverbanks, and no standing militia to resist a determined push. [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],The Minnesota Tribe]] has used that vulnerability well. Beneath the canopy, they've carved out staging grounds and hidden command centers, repurposing old survey bunkers and abandoned prefabs. "Commander {COMMANDER.Callsign}. Welcome to Horgens. The Tribe's presence here is light, but embedded. Forward depots, staging trails, relay points. Small anchors spread across an undeveloped world. You will break them one by one." The tactical overlay flashes. Three red markers highlight key sites. "One target is a supply convoy en route to a depot. You'll strike mid-transit. Cripple their logistics chain before it tightens." "Another is a regional command site under construction. Incomplete, exposed. Capture it before they finish bringing it online." "The third is a lone scout carrying sensitive data. They're attempting to reach extraction. Stop them. We need that intel." She returns her gaze to the Commander. "You will complete all three operations. This is just the first blow. Choose where to land." A pause. Her voice lowers slightly. "You'll have 14 days to begin. After each operation, you'll receive a bonus. Captured tech, equipment, supplies. The Watch does not waste success." The transmission cuts.

column1: The Argo enters orbit above Horgens III, the third planet in the system and barely more than a fledgling colony. Far below, dense lowland jungles and shallow coastal floodplains stretch between narrow strips of prefabricated structures, the earliest bones of a scattered, agrarian economy. Rainfall veils much of the surface, forming shifting fog banks that ripple through river deltas and cling to newly raised rooftops. There are no major cities here. No real defenses. Just scattered settlements clinging to humid ground, and the Tribe's hidden staging zones buried in the canopy. A secured Hyperpulse transmission arrives moments later. Mizuki Bekker's image flickers into view, her tone as measured as ever. "Horgens is more than just a humid backwater. It's becoming a nerve center for our expansion, and the [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bears]] know it. They've launched a multi-pronged push to destabilize everything we've built there." She brings up a flickering display of tactical readouts, one after the other. "First, we have a convoy hauling food and ammunition to a forward depot. It's ready to leave, but Watch ambushers are tightening their noose. You'll need to get that convoy through. Second, our command node, freshly established and still half-buried in the jungle, is under direct threat. They're planning a concentrated strike. If they breach that facility, the entire chain of coordination on Horgens collapses. And third, one of our scout teams went dark just hours ago. They were carrying sensitive base schematics. If they're captured, or silenced, our defenses are compromised before they've even solidified." She leans forward slightly, voice firm. "All three missions must be completed. But you choose where to begin. Once a contract is issued, it must be launched within fourteen days. Fail to act in time, and the window closes." A pause. "You will be rewarded after each strike. Weapons, tech, support assets, what we can spare. Just hold this ground. Every inch of it matters."

column1: The Argo is still preparing for travel when a proximity alert chirps on the bridge console. An unmarked shuttle, running cold with no transponder, slides into docking range without hailing. By the time Sumire calls it in, the shuttle has already latched to the cargo bay, deposited three sealed crates, and detached. No pilot visible through the canopy. No markings. No comm traffic. Yang pries the first crate open in the mech bay, crowbar in hand. He pulls back the foam lining and stops. "Well. At least they're paying in hardware." Inside, packed in impact-resistant cradles, is a set of components stamped with no manufacturer logos. The machining is tight. The alloy work is unfamiliar. Yang turns a stabilizer housing over in his hands, testing the weight. "Custom fabrication. Nothing off a standard production line. Whoever built this wasn't cutting corners." He sets it down carefully and moves to the second crate. "More of the same. Actuator assemblies, targeting linkages, heat management modules. All unmarked, all field-ready." Before he can open the third, Darius comes through the bay door at a half-jog, datapad in hand. "Commander. We just picked up a transmission. Tight-beam, Watch encryption. It's from Arelle." He holds up the datapad. The message is short, the language is not. "I won't read the whole thing out loud. Let's just say she found some creative uses for words I didn't think she knew. The short version is she knows we've turned, and she's promising to personally drag us back in pieces." Yang glances up from the crate. "That was fast." Darius nods, still scanning the message. "Faster than it should have been. Either someone told her or she is tracking the Argo's energy fluctuations from preparing for travel. Either way, she's not guessing. She knows." The bay falls quiet for a moment. Yang looks at the open crates, then back at Darius. "Well. New boss sends gifts, old boss sends death threats. At least we know where we stand."

column1: The Argo settles into high orbit over a scorched, wind-blasted world in the Star Cluster 752 system. Below lies Merovi, a desolate, sand-choked planet littered with decaying Star League ruins. Bunkers, towers, and broken relay stations half-consumed by time now serve a new master: the Minnesota Tribe. From these fractured strongholds, they coordinate raids and dig in. A Hyperpulse transmission arrives as the crew finishes system checks. Star Colonel Arelle Jorgensson appears at the holotable, her tone clipped and focused. "Commander {COMMANDER.Callsign}. Welcome to Star Cluster 752. The Tribe has embedded itself in multiple positions across the surface. All must be eliminated." A tactical map lights up with three key targets. "One is a combat staging zone, dug in and defended. No objectives but the enemy. You'll make contact, break their line, and erase everything breathing. Another is a buried [[DM.Factions[faction_SLDF],SLDF]] relay. They've been using it for long-range coordination. Now they're trying to wipe it before we reach it. You'll recover the data and shut them down. The third is a logistics redoubt. Not fully fortified yet, but once it is, they'll use it to resupply and repair forward elements across the region. Take it before they do." She folds her arms. "You will complete all three. This is not about choice, only sequence. You have 14 days to begin the one you select. After each, you'll be rewarded. Advanced tech, recovered gear, surplus resources." "Choose your first strike, Commander." The transmission ends.

column1: The Argo drops out of its final jump into the Fröislandis system, deep in the [[DM.BaseDescriptionDefs[LoreAntiSpinward],anti-spinward]] sector of the [[DM.BaseDescriptionDefs[LoreDeepPeriphery],Deep Periphery]] past the Cygnus Loop. Sensors immediately begin sweeping the frozen planet below. Marcus Hammerick's face appears on the viewscreen before anyone can speak. His expression is grim. "Commander {COMMANDER.Callsign}, the tactical situation is more complex than we anticipated. Joanna has fortified the facility with multiple defensive layers. You'll need to execute a two-phase assault with no pause between operations." "Phase One is breaching the outer perimeter defenses. Joanna has deployed her most fanatical [[DM.Factions[faction_RemembranceCell],Remembrance Cell]] warriors to guard the facility approaches. Elite guards who know the terrain and are prepared to die protecting what they believe is their people's salvation. You must destroy these forces completely to gain access to the inner facility." "Phase Two begins the moment the outer perimeter falls. You will immediately assault the Armageddon production facility itself where the prototype is being held. There is no time to regroup or repair. The moment Joanna realizes her outer defenses have failed, she will deploy the Armageddon mech and throw every remaining warrior at you." "This is a continuous operation. Breach the perimeter, then immediately push into the facility without stopping. If you give Joanna time to prepare, she may escape with the prototype or technical data. You cannot allow that." Sumire pulls up the tactical data. "Frozen world with significant sensor interference. Limited visibility from atmospheric conditions and constant snowfall. And we're conducting two consecutive assaults with no recovery time between them." Darius looks grim. "Boss, this is going to push us past our limits. Two full engagements back to back in terrible conditions against fanatics who believe they're fighting for their survival." Farah reviews the data. "We have Dr. Tilsaye's complete technical specifications. We know the facility layout, the defensive systems, the weapon capabilities. That intelligence advantage matters, but we'll be exhausted by the time we reach the inner facility." Yang checks ammunition reserves. "We'll be running on fumes by the second assault. Better make the first one count." Marcus's expression becomes even more serious, almost haunted. "Commander, now that we are at the point of no return, I need you to understand something. I have acquired a two hundred gigaton nuclear warhead. The only delivery method for a warhead of this magnitude is ramming a DropShip directly into the surface at terminal velocity. I have a vessel prepared for that purpose." Yang's face goes pale. "Two hundred gigaton." Marcus nods with a guilty expression."If it detonates, the blast will consume everything within hundreds of kilometers. The thermal pulse will be visible from orbit. Fröislandis VII's ice caps will flash-boil. The planetary surface will be permanently scarred." "If the conventional assault fails and there is any risk of Joanna escaping with the prototype technology or technical data, I will order that DropShip to ram the facility and detonate on impact." "Everyone at Fröislandis VII dies in that scenario. Myself and all my forces. Your company. Every Remembrance Cell fanatic. Even the Argo if it's anywhere near the surface point of impact. The small research outpost on the planet with innocent researchers. Everything. The planet itself will bear the scars for centuries." "The Armageddon weapon's technology cannot be allowed to survive if we cannot secure it for destruction. I am willing to sacrifice everyone there, including myself, to ensure this weapon does not reach deployment status." "You need to win, Commander. You need to destroy that weapon before I have to make that choice. Because if you fail, I will detonate that warhead. I will kill everyone on that planet, including you and your crew. Win at any cost. There is no other option. Good luck and godspeed, Commander. If this fails, there won't be anyone left to bury the dead." The transmission ends abruptly. Silence fills the command deck. No one moves. No one speaks.

<color=#BFBFBF>The screen hums, still displaying the Ghost Bear emblem over a planet you just left.

Whatever's happening out there. The masks are starting to slip.</color>

column1: The Argo's command deck is crowded but focused. Marcus Hammerick and Dr. Tilsaye appear on split viewscreens. Darius speaks first. "Marcus, Dr. Tilsaye. Joanna contacted us directly. She knows we have the archive and she knows Dr. Tilsaye is no longer in her custody. During the confrontation she let something slip. She mentioned Fröislandis VII. We believe that's where the weapon is located." Marcus's expression shifts immediately. "Fröislandis VII. Even deeper into the Periphery. That has to be where she's completing final assembly." Dr. Tilsaye speaks up, her expression grave. "Before we discuss tactical plans, you need to understand what the Armageddon project actually is. The designation is misleading. Armageddon is a complete weapons platform. A mech." "An enormous superheavy mech, far larger than any BattleMech successfully constructed in human history. Previous superheavy designs were limited to approximately two hundred tons due to structural and materials constraints. This prototype exceeds that limit by a significant margin. The breakthrough came from exotic materials research. Lattice-core structural supports, rapid-form reinforcement systems. All the research Joanna forced me to complete. This is why she needed me specifically." "The prototype also incorporates Project Rotating Fury, a parallel weapons program I was never cleared to access. The security classification was higher than anything else in the Armageddon archive. Be extremely careful, Commander." Yang breaks the silence. "A mech past the two hundred ton threshold? The structural stress alone would be catastrophic. You're telling us she built something that shouldn't be able to function?" Tilsaye nods slowly. "The exotic materials solve problems that made superheavy combat units of this scale impossible before. Whether it functions as designed under combat conditions, I cannot guarantee. But Joanna believes it works. She's staking everything on that belief." Marcus takes over. "Intelligence points to Joanna activating the weapon ahead of schedule. With the archive gone and Dr. Tilsaye extracted, she's forcing her remaining researchers to accelerate final assembly. Completion is possible within days. At the same time she's pulling every [[DM.Factions[faction_RemembranceCell],Remembrance Cell]] warrior back from across the Deep Periphery. Every fanatic who believes in her vision. The facility will be heavily defended." "We need to get to Fröislandis VII before she can deploy that weapon against a major population center. Or worse, before she proves the concept and starts building more. This prototype cannot be allowed to survive." "Fröislandis VII is a small frozen planet at the edge of the system. Polar ice caps, tundra biomes. Extreme cold, low visibility, atmospheric interference on sensors. Heat dissipation will be excellent, but mobility and targeting will suffer." He pauses. "I've rallied what loyal Tribe warriors I could find who are willing to stand against her. A small force, nothing like her numbers, but it will have to be enough. Even I will be there." "Before you commit, I want you to know that we are opening our remaining supply caches to your unit. Weapons, equipment, ammunition, everything we have left. If we fail at Fröislandis VII none of it matters anyway. Consider it yours regardless of your decision." "I hope you will join us. You have already proved your combat capabilities and with your strength at our side we might stand a chance. Please accept this final contract, Commander. Let me know your decision as soon as you have one." The transmission ends. The crew looks to you for the decision.

column1: The bridge holotable lights up with a fresh transmission, sealed under full encryption. The identifier reads: Jorgensson, A. The image resolves slowly. Arelle stands at parade rest, her uniform pristine, her posture stiff. She doesn't offer a greeting. "Commander. Based on recent intelligence intercepts, we have isolated three key sites where the enemy is consolidating assets or infrastructure critical to their next phase of operations. Your unit is to proceed first to Eagle Rest. A hostile relay array has been embedded in legacy terraforming machinery and is suspected of coordinating encrypted off-world logistics. Afterward, you will be directed to Butzfleth Majoris and Cygnus III, in that order. Full details will be provided on arrival. Maintain strict operational silence. Continue to act under Watch directive. That is all." The feed cuts before anyone can speak. A beat of silence follows. Darius exhales slowly. "Well. That wasn't icy at all." Yang scratches behind his ear. "Did she even blink during that?" Sumire mutters, "Three jumps. Three systems. Across half a quadrant. In a rustbucket held together by duct tape and Farah's existential dread. Great." Farah doesn't look up from her data slate. "I'll prep the systems. A considerable number of jump sequences, and she's not budgeting any refit time between them. That's going to catch up with us." Darius glances at you. "You want to press forward, Commander? This starts with Eagle Rest. Once we jump... we're committed." You nod. The order's clear. The sentiment behind it? Less so. But the war moves on, and you're going with it.

column1: The bridge is quiet. Too quiet. Dr. Tilsaye was handed off to Tribe operatives two hours ago, still trembling, still whispering pleas that went unanswered. No one on the crew has said much since. Then the HPG relay chimes. Incoming transmission. Encrypted under Tribe protocols. Darius brings it up on the main display. Text only. No greeting. Just Joanna's signature cold efficiency. "Dr. Tilsaye has provided useful intelligence. A [[TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef,{TGT_SYSTEM.OwnerDef.Demonym}]] research complex has an archival facility here on Ryerson that houses historical records related to Clan Wolverine. Research Station Theta-7. The facility must be destroyed immediately. Complete data core elimination is required. No recovery must be possible. Coordinates attached. Proceed at once." The transmission ends. No explanation of methodology. No mention of Dr. Tilsaye's condition. Farah stares at the screen, her expression carefully neutral. "That was fast. We delivered her less than three hours ago." Sumire glances at the timestamp. "Very fast. Either she cooperated immediately or they were very persuasive." Yang grunts from his station. "Persuasive. Right. That's one word for it." Darius shifts uncomfortably. "Maybe they offered her something. Protection for remaining family. Financial compensation. Something that made cooperation worth it." Sumire's voice is flat. "Maybe. Or maybe they didn't need to offer anything at all." The silence stretches. Everyone knows what "persuasive" likely means when dealing with Joanna's operatives. No one wants to say it out loud. Farah finally breaks the tension. "The target coordinates are clear. Research Station Theta-7. If the intel is accurate, it's a legitimate military intelligence target this time." Darius nods slowly. "Records about Clan Wolverine operations. That's strategic intelligence. Worth securing or destroying, depending on which side you're on." Yang stands, stretching. "So we're torching a library now. Great. That'll look fantastic on the resume." Darius looks to you, waiting for the order. The coordinates are loaded. The mission is clear. But the method of intelligence acquisition hangs in the air like smoke.

column1: The databanks only have a small entry on the planet called Kuras Drift. It is a small, rocky planet in the outer edge of the Malador Cluster system. It lacks a stable atmosphere. Its surface is exposed to deep vacuum in most regions. However, gravitational interactions with the nearby gas giant Malador's Eye produce rare "tidal pockets" of loosely held atmospheric gases that gather temporarily in crater basins and lowland fractures. These pressure zones are weak and unstable, offering little more than temporary shelter from hard vacuum. Kuras Drift has no known settlements or structures. Its geological profile is harsh and ancient, consisting of fractured bedrock and deep impact scars. Though long ignored, recent scans suggest the presence of rare raw materials beneath the crust, and the planet has been marked by several large companies for possible future exploitation. [A flashpoint has been created in the Malador Cluster system for the next step of the campaign]

column1: The feed cuts to black. Sumire huffs and leans against the console, her tone biting. "What a bunch of sensationalist drivel. That 'general' looked like a recruitment poster got drunk and wandered into a news booth. But people'll eat it up." Farah closes the console slowly, arms crossed. "They released enough footage for the story to stick, not enough for any attribution. This wasn't a leak. Someone packaged this deliberately." Yang narrows his eyes at the final image. "Yeah, if INN's getting clean visuals like that, someone's either feeding them… or the Tribe's putting on a show. Making sure just enough leaks to stir the pot." Darius mutters, "INN stokes the fire, and when the blaze reaches us, nobody's gonna care which way the wind was blowing. Just who to burn." No one replies. Across the stars, fear is rising, and the mercs caught in the middle are now part of the story, whether they want to be or not. You take a deep breath, calming your nerves, before calling for the departure for Melidron immediately. Time is running out and Arelle better have a plan ready.

<color=#BFBFBF>The mess hall is louder than it's been in weeks. Laughter, clinking cups, exhausted sighs of relief. Victory buzzes in the air like static. The hulking war machine is gone. Against all odds, they won.

Sumire leans back in her chair, grinning.</color> "Still can't believe we dropped that walking mountain. Bet the whole damn planet felt it hit the ground."

<color=#BFBFBF>Yang scoffs through a mouthful of food.</color> "I felt it in my spine. Thing must've weighed more than an assault carrier."

<color=#BFBFBF>Even Farah allows herself a tired smile.</color> "And now… maybe this ends."

<color=#BFBFBF>But as the minutes tick by, the smiles begin to fade. No encrypted burst from Arelle. No update. No acknowledgment. Nothing.

Darius glances around the table, frowning.</color> "She should've said something by now. Even a one-line message."

<color=#BFBFBF>Farah checks her terminal again.</color> "No ping on her key. Nothing from the [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Watch]] core either."

<color=#BFBFBF>Yang mutters,</color> "Maybe she's off the grid now that her job's done. Pulled a vanishing act."

<color=#BFBFBF>Sumire's expression darkens.</color> "But the [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Tribe]]'s not done. They still hold systems. Why disappear now?"

<color=#BFBFBF>Suddenly an incoming transmission flashes on the main wall.</color>

<color=#DFDFDF>INCOMING: Ghost Bear Watch Command priority signal – Level Three Encryption Detected – No personal authorization key present.</color>

<color=#BFBFBF>Darius straightens instantly.</color> "That's not right."

<color=#BFBFBF>The room stills.</color>

column1: The screen flares to life with a burst of static, then clears to reveal Mizuki Bekker once again. Her tone is direct, sharpened by urgency. "Star Cluster 752 is now on the front line. We have three key objectives that must be completed in sequence. I will not mince words, each of these tasks is vital to preserving our hold on this world, and all of them will fall to you. First, we must intercept [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bear]] raiders on the way to our desert forward operations camp. Then, we need to recover sensitive data buried beneath the sands, data the Ghost Bears would use to overwhelm our defenses. Finally, the planet's main logistics redoubt must be defended at all costs. If it falls, our operational reach collapses." She pauses, gaze intense. "You choose the order. But know this: once issued, each contract must be launched within two weeks. Delay, and the opportunity, and the advantage, is lost. After each success, a small cache will be provided. Weapons, custom tech, ammunition, tools to keep you in the fight." She leans forward slightly. "This is where we make our stand. Choose your next strike."

column1:
<color=#BFBFBF>The shuttle arrives exactly when Arelle said it would. No transponder, no hail, no pilot visible through the canopy. It docks, offloads three crates onto the cargo bay floor, and detaches before Sumire can even log the approach vector.</color>

<color=#BFBFBF>Yang is already in the bay with a pry bar before the docking clamps finish cycling.</color>

<color=#BFBFBF>He cracks the first crate and goes still.</color>

"That's an XL engine. Clan-spec. The heat shielding alone on this thing is worth more than most of our mechs."

<color=#BFBFBF>He runs a hand along the housing, checking the seams.</color> "No production stamps. No serial numbers. Whoever built this didn't want it traced. But the machining is clean. This is front-line hardware."

<color=#BFBFBF>The second and third crates open easier. Packed in shock-dampened cradles, four ER PPCs sit in matched pairs, barrel shrouds still sealed in factory wrap.</color>

"Clan extended range PPCs, four of them."

<color=#BFBFBF>Yang steps back and looks at the open crates, hands on his hips.</color>

"I'll say this for the Star Colonel. She knows how to make an introduction."

<color=#BFBFBF>He reaches into the third crate and pulls out a sealed envelope tucked against the packing foam. Plain paper. Handwritten. He reads it once, then holds it up.</color>

"There's a note. Signed by Jorgensson herself."

<color=#DFDFDF>"Commander. These are yours regardless of what follows. But understand this clearly. If you entertain the thought of playing both sides, I will know before you have finished thinking it. Do not test me on this.

—Star Colonel Arelle Jorgensson"</color>

<color=#BFBFBF>Darius appears at the bay entrance, arms crossed.</color> "So that's what good faith looks like from the Watch. Clan-grade weapons and a power plant that could run a small city."

<color=#BFBFBF>Yang hands him the note. Darius reads it and exhales slowly.</color>

"Gifts and threats in the same crate. At least she's efficient."

<color=#BFBFBF>Yang shrugs.</color> "Could be worse."

column1: The transmission from Arelle Jorgensson ends with a hard cut. No thank you, no farewell. Just silence. And the faint hum of the Argo's systems. Darius exhales through his nose, arms crossed. "This is spiraling. Fast. We're talking coordinated strikes against a rogue Clan... and she expects us to be the tip of the spear?" Sumire leans against the console, glancing toward the viewport. "And if we say no? What happens then? She doesn't strike me as the 'let bygones be bygones' type." Yang grunts. "The [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bear Watch]] doesn't leave debts unsettled. And she sees this whole thing as a matter of blood and honor. If we bail now, we don't just walk. We run. And we keep running." Farah taps her datapad with restless fingers. "We're in deeper than salvage and payouts now. This is something else. Old ghosts. Buried wars. And one misstep could light the whole thing off." No one speaks for a long moment. Eventually, all eyes shift to you, the commander. Darius speaks again, voice low. "Look... you've gotten us through worse than this. We trust you, {COMMANDER.Callsign}. Just tell us where we're going." Whatever comes next, strike deep or vanish into the black, they'll follow. But the weight of that choice presses heavier than ever.

<color=#BFBFBF>The waiting stretches on. Quiet, watchful. No new pings, no scheduled updates. Just long-range scans and standard monitoring protocols.

Then, an identification signal appears. Not broadcast. Buried. Encoded in a tight envelope using the same Tribe cipher Mizuki once shared, and routed through a degraded relay deep in McEvedy's Folly's orbital junkfield.

Farah picks it up instantly.</color> "We've got something incoming. They identified using the same Tribe encryption as last time."

<color=#BFBFBF>Moments later, the proximity alert pings. A compact shuttle, no markings, no chatter, rises over the horizon and burns toward the Argo.

No weapons. No transponder. No instructions. It docks without asking.

Airlock cycle: fast. A single figure boards, cloaked, helmeted, silent. They carry a sealed crate. No introduction, no ceremony. The figure places the crate just inside the corridor, gives a single nod, and vanishes back through the airlock before anyone speaks.

Sumire mutters from the upper deck.</color> "Friendly types, aren't they?"

<color=#BFBFBF>The crate is sealed but untrapped.  Inside: a dense, ruggedized encryption unit, low EM profile, thermally shielded, and covered in unfamiliar diagnostic ports. A slight humming can be heard from its insides.

She crouches beside the crate, tools in hand.</color> "This isn't standard crypto gear. It's layered. Already semi-active. Whatever protocol this is... it's beyond anything I've seen. It's not just secure, it's engineered to keep everything else from even knowing it exists."

column1: Weeks pass aboard the Argo in tense quiet. Contracts roll in, systems get overhauled, the crew drifts back into the routines of downtime, yet no one quite relaxes. The [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Minnesota Tribe]] has gone dark since the last campaign. No broadcasts. No incursions. No retaliation. That changes with the arrival of a sealed transmission, stamped Classified: Watch Cipher Omega-Black. One of the most secure protocols Arelle has provided, requiring a multi-part decryption key with biometric components. The attached [[DM.Factions[faction_GhostBearWatch],Ghost Bear Watch]] briefing is meticulous and alarming. The Minnesota Tribe has launched a major coordinated operation, designated Operation Cobra Strike. Without warning, they seized control of several colony worlds far closer to the Inner Sphere than their previous holdings, some within jump distance of major trade corridors. Each strike unfolded with surgical precision: small units, heavy tonnage, zero warning. From these footholds, they initiated a synchronized wave of deep raids across multiple sectors. Munitions depots. Forward command posts. Sensor networks. Even limited strikes within the borders of the Great Houses. The timing of each hit was near-perfect, and the identity of the attackers remained ambiguous long enough to paralyze defenses. According to the Watch, these raids completely bypassed the outer systems the crew had helped retake. Horgens, Star Cluster 752, Rim Worlds Republic Outpost #11. All untouched. The Watch seems to have no explanation for how they slipped past Ghost Bear lines without triggering alarms. False transponder codes. Repainted hulls. Silent jumps. It's clear the Tribe's veil of secrecy has not only held. It's gotten stronger. As Darius scans the report, his jaw tightens. "This wasn't a reaction. It was well prepared. And we're behind again." He glances toward the comms array. "We better head back to Melidron. I bet we're going to hear from Arelle soon."

column1: You return to your quarters late, expecting a few system reports and a half-charged sleep cycle. Instead, your personal datapad is flashing. A new message, with the Subject FOR YOUR EYES ONLY. No senders listed. No traceable headers. Just a single embedded file. Against your better judgment, you open it. It's text-only. No signature. No voice. But you recognize the cadence instantly, and the symbol at the bottom removes all doubt: the crest of the [[DM.Factions[faction_MinnesotaTribe],Minnesota Tribe]]. "You didn't believe me when I told you what the Ghost Bears are willing to hide. But now you've seen it firsthand. Your handler has admitted to violating her own Clan's command structure. She has endangered your outfit, your reputation, and your future for her own crusade. And she never told you why. I would like to speak again. This time, I will bring you more of the truth. Things Arelle will never tell you. Speak to no one before deciding. This offer is only for you." You read it twice. Then a third time. She knows. About the call with Arelle. The 4 billion. The confession. You haven't spoken to anyone outside the crew. That message was buried in encrypted transmission layers. And yet... Mizuki knows. You consider your options.

column1: A Bondsman was a prisoner taken during combat by a Clan, of any caste or rank, who was held as an indentured servant. Bondsmen were bound by tradition, rather than chains, to work dutifully for their new masters. For a bondsman to purposefully neglect their responsibilities or even attempt escape stained not just their personal honor but the honor of their original Clan. Typically, a bondsman would either be released from their bond and sent back home, with little honor lost, or after a given period of time, be adopted and become a free, full member of their new Clan. When and whether an individual was released from their servitude varied between Clans and individuals: some only spent a token amount of time before being freed from their bondscord, while others would live out the rest of their lives as bondsmen.

column1: A breakthrough in plasma-based weapon augmentation, Thermo-Electro-Magnetic Plasma Energy Synchronization Transducers (TEMPEST) are advanced manifolds developed by the Minnesota Tribe to regulate and exploit the thermal and electromagnetic output of specialized fusion cores, particularly the Magnothermic Plasma Engine. Integrated into PPCs, flamers, plasma rifles, and TSEMP systems, TEMPEST units channel superheated plasma into the weapon discharge matrix, dramatically increasing both kinetic and thermal impact. While the plasma stream briefly aids in weapon-cycle cooling, each activation adds a stacking thermal load that gradually overwhelms even the most powerful heat sinks. Prolonged use rapidly escalates internal heat levels, risking system overload and shutdown. Despite these dangers, the raw firepower TEMPEST provides has made it a hallmark of the Tribe’s heaviest frontline units.

column1:
A cunning and ruthless dictator, Majorian was the first non-O'Reilly to ever reign over the Marian Hegemony. Majorian's road to power differed little from that of the O'Reilly family, rising from a high-ranking position and launching a coup d'état. Once in power, Majorian killed or exiled the bulk of the O'Reilly family to prevent them from reclaiming the throne.

Drunk on power, Majorian began a policy of expansion into the faltering Free Worlds League, often deriding the once great Successor State as little more than "free real estate". Majorian's cruelty did not go unnoticed, and eventually brought about an open war with Clan Wolf.

The war with Wolf went poorly and, in order to make peace, Majorian was forced to abdicate his throne and become a bondsman to the Clan.

Majorian's bondsmanship lasted several years before he was able to free himself. With the Clan distracted by other issues, Majorian quietly slipped back into the Hegemony and quickly rebuilt support. He forced Hans O'Reilly out, making him flee to the Circinus Federation.

Majorian quickly renewed his warmongering, launching a conquest of the neighboring Magistracy of Canopus. Catching the Magistracy largely unprepared, the Hegemony ultimately conquered much of Canopus despite support from numerous allies bolstering the MAF.

Majorian's rule went unimpeded for several years, until Hans O'Reilly returned with forces from the Circinus Federation and launched a surprise operation to put himself back on the throne. Unfortunately for the pirates, the Marian forces seemed to have had some warning of the invasion and were well-prepared, repelling the pirates and pushing them back in a counter-invasion. Ultimately, this cost the Federation large portions of its Illyrian and Lothorian conquests.

After forcing the pirates to peace terms that favored the Marians, Majorian would reach his crowning achievement when the infuriated High-Khan Fiona Kerensky of Clan Wolf delivered a batchall via a large marble slab dropped from orbit onto the emperor's palace. It is said that the slab very nearly killed the malevolent ruler when it destroyed his favorite bathroom - which he had been in just minutes before.

Majorian accepted the High-Khan's batchall and prepped himself for personal combat with the Khan and her second. While Majorian himself was a rather average MechWarrior, his second, Somaru was, unfortunately for the Khan, one of the most skilled MechWarriors to have ever been born. Somaru proceeded to decisively win the batchall and, from there on out, few would challenge the now power-drunk emperor.

While elements of the MAF would eventually reclaim large portions of the the former Canopian territory, Majorian's Marian Hegemony remained cemented as the major power in the rimward Inner Sphere for many years to come.

Unfortunately for the emperor himself, his reign was cut short. After ruling the Hegemony for a grand total of 58 years, Majorian found himself slain by his second, as Somaru seized power for himself just after Majorian had finished teaching him everything he knew.

Darius, watching you, says, "{COMMANDER.FirstName}, why don't we find another watering hole? Some place a little quieter for the story you need to tell."

Later that night, as you finish your tale, the table is covered with empty glasses and the lights are low.

Darius finally leans back and furrows his brow. "I can't pretend to understand the pressures of the nobility, that's for sure. And no matter your regrets, you can't change the past. But you can make a better place for the family that we have up there in orbit."

He raises a glass and together you toast the future.

As the officer finishes her comm call, storm clouds gather in her face. It's the same look you see on a MechWarrior after you've delivered a solid dressing-down.

"Commander," she says without the smug tone she exhibited earlier. "I've been directed by my superiors to let you go. Please accept my..." You can almost taste the sour lemon in her mouth, "My apologies for inconveniencing you."

As you board the transports and continue your journey to the secret location of the Black Market, Darius finally breaks out into a satisfied smile. "Well played, Commander. This will make a good story for the crew."

As you enter the bridge you see a pair of astechs leaving after installing the console over in Navigation.

You walk over to where Sumire is standing next to the console, "So, is it ready?"

Sumire turns to you, "Well, it is the moment of truth Commander.  The console has power and is ready to be turned on."

You motion to the power switch, "It's your project.  The honours are yours."

Sumire reaches out and pushes the button on the console.  An audible click sounds, along with a number of whirring fans.  The console's screen flickers before focusing and revealing the display where a large blinking <color=#FF0000>ACTIVATE?</color> pulses.

Sumire looks at you, "It appears to be working so far, Commander.  You should be the one to activate it."

"I've heard back from two potential customers in {TGT_SYSTEM.Name} orbit. One would pay cash for the fresh food. I think I can get ¢75,000, give or take. The other is offering machine tools in trade, which the Mech Bay could use to boost productivity."

As you leave the bar on [[TGT_SYSTEM,{TGT_SYSTEM.Name}]], a cloaked figure cautiously steps in front of you, "Hey, I have something you may be interested in buying."

You wave the figure away as you step around them, "No thanks, not interested."

The cloaked figure moves to lean casually against the wall, "I have heard you are under the scrutiny of the Commercial JumpShip Transit Authority and only want to offer you a way to make their investigation of you disappear."

You stop and turn towards the figure, "What's the catch?  What is in it for you?"

The figure laughs, "C-Bills of course, what else?  Look, I have a single use access code which will allow you to log into the CJSTA server and delete any flags assocatied with you or {COMPANY.CompanyName}. For a measly sum of ¢2,500,000."

You whistle, "That's a bit steep is it not?"

The figure smiles, "Enjoy paying those fines they will continue to issue to you.  Who knows, perhaps you will be lucky enough to find a hacker willing to help you one day.  I can assure you, they will cost more to do the same job."

You contemplate the offer...

column1:
Baelin "Braver" Hawker was one of Clan Diamond Shark's most prestigious Khans. Over the course of his khanship, Braver expanded the size and power of the 'Merchant Clan', taking full advantage of the Sharks' mercantile and military prowess in equal measure.

A true Clan warrior at heart, Braver went out of his way to make sure any battle was fought with honor, even purposefully bidding away advantages his Clan held in order to ensure a fair fight.

Ultimately, like most Diamond Sharks', Braver's dream was to open a great market on Terra, a goal he dedicated his life to. Armed with simulations that showed to other Clans that he could make such dreams a reality - if the Clans invaded under his leadership - Braver was eventually elected to the position of ilKhan, the only Diamond Shark ever honored this way.

column1: Bearing the weight of the McEvedy name is no easier task and, perhaps, it was particularly difficult for young Talulah. A rebellious and stubborn soul, Talulah was widely seen as a spoiled brat who enjoyed breaking the law; in fact, her application to MechWarrior training came as a surprise to many and was actually rejected twice due to outstanding legal cases. Born on New Avalon to one of the Federated Suns' most respected noble families, it was clear from a young age that Ianaandru was a gifted and charismatic speaker. School records from his preschool indicate he regularly made deals and trades with his peers, getting them to do what he wanted without giving up much in return. Such charisma did not go unnoticed by House Davion, and Ianaandru quickly found himself fast-tracked through a prestigious military academy where he graduated at the top of his class (by making deals with his teachers, if some rumors are to be believed), and landed a high-ranking post within the AFFS diplomatic corps.

Here Ianaandru's skills found themselves put to good use, and only a few years later he found himself promoted to the head of the corps. Since then, Ianaandru has greatly expanded the size and reach of the corps, opening diplomatic relations with virtually every major and minor power or faction he can find. Ianaandru is so fond of diplomatic wheeling and dealing that AFFS records note he has even tried to open diplomatic relations with an advanced Star League era AI known as 'Roguebot', and an Elder God known as 'The Server Overlord'.

Born on Royal Foxx to an influential Canopian family, DeVega grew up in a privileged environment and luxury of extremes for the Periphery nation. Unfortunately, like most of his peers, DeVega let this fortune go to his head and fill him with privileged ideas and plans, none of which would come to pass.

Enrolling in the best academies that money and prestige could buy didn't matter. The Star League fell, and the wars that occurred leading to that claimed his family before seeing him join the SLDF for vengeance upon Amaris for what his schemes caused.

What was surprising was DeVega's ability in point-blank 'Mech brawling. Quickly rising to command a company, the numerous city fights saw him taking his signature Black Knight into brutal close-range combat.

When the war ended and the SLDF left, DeVega went with them. With no home to return to, he joined the Exodus and left the Inner Sphere behind for what he assumed would be a new life. But even in Exile, the SLDF faced war, so once more, he left a home behind.

The Clans were where he finally settled. Joining Clan Wolf, he earned the position of Star Colonel during the initial Trials, and after the Founder disappeared he was chosen to be Khan. Viewing people as one of their most valuable resources, it was not long before he came into conflict with other Clans, resulting first in a victorious absorption of Smoke Jaguar, then yet another Exodus - this time back to the Inner Sphere.

With several colonial territories established, Clan Wolf fought in war after war, and numerous Trials. Making allies and enemies alike, Clan Wolf under his leadership flourished, culminating in a climactic Trial of Possession for Terra itself. A Trial that saw the Wolf once again the victors, and his taking the title of ilKhan.

column1:
Born on the world of Lone Star, Glyndwr Gunvald grew up dreaming of the knights of ancient Terra and their battles. Born to a family with long-held military traditions, Glyndwr's mother served as a MechWarrior within the elite Royal Divisions of the SLDF, and his father was a well-respected MechTech in the standard SLDF corps.

With an upbringing like this, it is little wonder that Glyndwr eventually came to see MechWarriors as the modern incarnation of the knights of legend and aspired to become one of them. To further this goal, Glyndwr studied hard, eventually applying to and getting accepted to the War Academy of Mars. Glyndwr graduated several years later, ranking amongst the top of his class and immediately accepted a role with the 218th Royal Light Horse Regiment.

Being one of the few to survive the destruction of the unit during the Periphery Uprising, Glyndwr was assigned to independent operations within the occupied Terran Hegemony. Smuggled onto worlds with the goal of helping organize local Hegemony garrison survivors, Glyndwr was assigned the new callsign "Liquidforce" to help keep his identity a secret from Amaris soldiers.

By the end of the war, he had served in campaigns to liberate or organize uprisings on 28 different Hegemony worlds, participating in the battle for Unity city itself on Terra.

While most of the SLDF eventually left with General Kerensky, Glyndwr opted to stay behind, having become more determined than ever to see the Hegemony restored to its former glory. Now serving under Lauren Hayes, Glyndwr would become one of the founding members of the Com Guard, helping organize and execute operation Silver Shield.

Throughout the First Succession War, the Com Guard took advantage of Glyndwr's experience to carry out many small but meaningful operations that required the skills he had obtained over the course of the Amaris crisis. This led Glyndwr all over known space, sometimes operating as a mercenary or infiltrating the military command of various states, all with the goal of furthering ComStar's strategic interests.

Towards the end of his active career, the now aging Glyndwr assumed the role of training the next generation of Com Guard operatives, and it would be his students that would eventually go on to carry out much of operation Holy Shroud.

While it has never been confirmed, some documents unearthed centuries later by Chandrasekhar Kurita suggest that Glyndwr may have also been a founding member of what would eventually become the Word of Blake.

Brilliant, unconventional, and heretic. These are all words used to describe Fiona Kerensky, the so-called "High-Khan" of Clan Wolf. An inheritor of the fabled Kerensky Bloodname - tracing back to Nicholas Kerensky himself - Fiona was born and raised in a typical Wolf sibko.

However, Fiona was destined to become anything but typical. Considered a ristar within the Clan, Fiona rose to the khanship of the Clan younger than any before her. What followed has been described as the golden age of Clan Wolf - or its darkest time, depending on who you talk to.

Despite coming from the bloodline of the founder himself, Fiona greatly resented the way the Clans were stuck in their traditions: too rigid and afraid of change, keeping from becoming truly great. Seeking to correct this, Fiona caused a great uproar amongst the Clans when she took the title "High-Khan", and immediately appointed a second saKhan. While many Clans, including the mighty Clan Ghost Bear, decried this very un-clanlike behavior, they were unable to do much as Clan Wolf set out along the exodus corridor towards the Inner Sphere.

Reaching the Inner Sphere, and mostly forsaking the Clan tradition of zellbrigen, Clan Wolf soon built itself a mighty empire by carving out large regions of the Draconis Combine and the Free Worlds League.

Fiona's high point was her rise to the status of ilKhan after the Wolves took temporary control of Terra. While the Ghost Bears and several other Clans denounced the feat upon learning that the Wolves had bargained for temporary control instead of winning it through conquest, they proved unable to stop Fiona's rise.

From here, sadly, the fortunes of Wolf and Fiona began to turn. The Wolves lost stewardship of Strana Mechty to the Ghost Bears, and much of their empire within the doomed DC was lost. Nowhere is the ultimate fate of Fiona recorded - some say the Wolves were brayed by the mad Emperor Majorian and his right-hand Somaru in a batchall, others say Fiona simply ruled the remains of the Wolf Empire until eventually another challenger successfully won khanship from her. Yet others say she simply disappeared altogether.

What is known is that after her rule of the Clan ended, the Wolves largely returned to Clan traditions and mostly tried to bury the history of Fiona. However, in some circles her unconventional ways are still remembered and held dear, with some promising to bring back the ways of the High-Khan, should they ever be in the position to do so.
